bib.title: Proposer-Agent-Evaluator (PAE): Autonomous Skill Discovery for Foundation Model Internet Agents

read.skipped: Reference list lines ~1100-1200 only skimmed; figure images (trajectory screenshots) are not text.

question: Can foundation-model agents autonomously propose, practice and evaluate their own tasks with RL so that the learned skills zero-shot transfer to human-written tasks and unseen websites?
hypothesis: VLMs are better at proposing tasks and judging outcomes than at acting, so reliable proposer/evaluator signals can bootstrap agent skill beyond what the proposer/evaluator itself achieves.
contributions: PAE: a learning system with a context-aware task proposer, an agent policy and an image-based autonomous outcome evaluator, trained with online RL
Design choices: website-name or user-demo context for the proposer, final-screenshot 0/1 outcome reward, an extra chain-of-thought reasoning step before each action
Zero-shot gains on WebVoyager and WebArena Easy and on 85 unseen websites; open-source SOTA 22.6% to 33.0% on WebVoyager

method.summary: A frozen VLM task proposer (Claude 3 Sonnet, or Qwen2VL as ablation) generates tasks from website context; a LLaVa-1.6 agent (SFT warm-started) attempts them in a browser with set-of-marks screenshots and emits thought then action; a frozen VLM judges the final three screenshots plus answer for a 0/1 reward; Filtered BC (NLL on successful trajectories) updates the policy each global iteration.

other.roles: task proposer, evaluator, SFT trajectory source, baseline

training.objective: Filtered Behavior Cloning: NLL imitation of thoughts and actions in successful (reward 1) trajectories; sparse 0/1 outcome reward
training.epochs: actor updates epochs per iteration: 4 (WebVoyager), 2 (WebArena Easy)

other.SFT warm-up: before RL on Claude trajectories (Appendix E)
other.trajectories to convergence: learning curves reach roughly 20K to 30K trajectories (read from Fig 3, Fig 6)
other.hyperparameter sensitivity: authors say PAE is relatively not sensitive to the three PAE-specific hyperparameters

inference.samples: one trajectory per task; PAE results are a running average of evaluation results at each iteration
inference.prompting: set-of-marks screenshot observation, thought then action format, max 10 steps per episode (15 steps stated in the WebArena prompt)

parameters.proposer context: website name only, or 10 user-demo screenshots per website (prompt appends 3 screenshots)
parameters.evaluator inputs: final three screenshots + agent final answer, binary SUCCESS / NOT SUCCESS

other.step limit conflict: Sec 4.1 says maximum 10 steps; Fig 18 WebArena prompt says 'You may have 15 steps'

metrics.name: Success rate
metrics.definition: fraction of tasks completed; WebVoyager ground truth by human annotation (tables use Claude Sonnet 3 auto-annotation, human alignment in Fig 4); WebArena Easy by functional verifiers; average weighted by task count

eval.protocol: Single reported run per cell; no seeds, variance or significance test; real websites change over time. Human study: 200 trajectories per method, 5 annotators.

availability.data: authors say they will release the full trajectory dataset

prompts.text: You are an expert in evaluating the performance of a web navigation agent. The agent is designed to help a human user navigate a website to complete a task. Your goal is to decide whether the agent’s execution is successful or not.
We are training a model to navigate the web. We need your help to generate instructions.
Imagine you are a robot browsing the web, just like humans. Now you need to complete a task.

limits: Open-source VLMs hallucinate too much to serve as evaluators in the headline setting; the main results rely on Claude 3 Sonnet as proposer and evaluator (Appendix G).
PAE models remain inferior to proprietary models such as Claude 3.5 Sonnet (Appendix G).
Real websites change over time so results may not reproduce exactly (Appendix G; Table 1 caption).
SFT warm-start from Claude 3 Sonnet trajectories is needed because open-source base agents score near 0 and give no reward; the PAE gain is measured over that SFT, not over zero-shot.
WebArena Easy is a subset with authors rewritten easier tasks on two sites; GitLab and CMS excluded.
No seeds, variance or significance tests reported; no compute or hardware stated; optimizer not stated.
Scope is web navigation only; extension to other domains is future work.

code.snippet: Initialize policy pi from a pre-trained checkpoint. Initialize replay buffer D. Obtain proposal task distribution C^(z_M). for each global iteration: for each trajectory: sample c ~ C^(z_M); roll out a_t ~ pi(.|s_t,c); r_t <- R^(s_t,a_t,c) if done else 0; D <- D U {(s_t,a_t,r_t,s_t+1,c)}; pi <- RL_update(pi, D)
